The dictionary explains the correct usage of each word.
reflect: to show or express something; to send back light, heat or sound
The essay should reflect your own opinions, not just the textbook's.
corruption: a change that makes something less pure or correct
sự biến dạng, sai lệch (ngôn ngữ)
The word's spelling is a corruption of an older French term.
via: They traveled to the island via a small ferry boat.
folk: relating to the traditional culture of ordinary people
The village still performs folk dances during the harvest festival.
etymology: the origin and history of a word
The etymology of the word 'salary' traces back to salt trade.
words: It has no words for kitchen tools or playground arguments any more.
mangrow: an old English word, possibly combined with 'grove' to form 'mangrove'
Etymologists link the old word mangrow to the modern term mangrove.
grove: They had a picnic under the shade of an olive grove.
according: in a way that agrees with or depends on something
Pay varies according to experience and the hours worked.
hogarth: Hogarth's classification of mangrove species is widely cited.
recognized: formally acknowledged or identified as already known
The team was recognized for its outstanding contribution to the mission.
about: The lecture was about how cities cope with extreme heat.
genera: groups of related species in biological classification
Botanists classified the new flowers into three separate genera.
constitute: form or make up a whole
These three departments constitute the entire management team.
true: in accordance with fact; genuine or accurate
The true figure is a great deal smaller.
exclusively: The species is found exclusively in this small mountain range.
habitats: the natural homes of animals or plants
Wetlands provide habitats for thousands of migrating birds.
demonstrating: showing clearly through action or example
The athlete kept training, demonstrating remarkable dedication to the sport.
many: Many residents still remember the flood of that year.
found: They found an old map hidden inside the wall.
similar: resembling something else without being identical
Her opinion on the matter is similar to mine.
solutions: ways of solving problems or dealing with difficult situations
The team brainstormed several solutions to the traffic problem.
variable: a factor or quantity that can change or vary
Temperature is an important variable in this experiment.
inundation: Coastal towns face growing risk of inundation as sea levels rise.
anaerobic: happening without oxygen, or not needing oxygen
Anaerobic bacteria thrive deep in the oxygen-poor mud.
soils: types or areas of the top layer of earth in which plants grow
Different crops thrive in different types of soils.
intense: very strong, extreme, or serious in degree
The competition between the two companies grew increasingly intense.
sunlight: light that comes from the sun
The room was flooded with warm sunlight in the afternoon.
biodiversity: the variety of plant and animal life in an area
The rainforest supports an extraordinary level of biodiversity.
generally: People generally prefer shorter commutes to work.
low: not high in level, amount or position
Prices stayed low throughout most of the summer.
given: provided or handed over to someone
Every student was given a copy of the new textbook.
occurs: Rust occurs when metal is exposed to moisture and air.
southeast: the direction or region midway between south and east
They spent a month backpacking around Southeast Asia.
particularly: especially, more than usual or more than others
The traffic gets particularly bad on Friday evenings near the bridge.
indonesian: The Indonesian archipelago contains thousands of separate islands.
archipelago: a group of many islands scattered in an area of sea
Tourists sailed through the archipelago to visit hidden beaches.
red: of the colour of blood or fire
She painted the front door a bright shade of red.
rhizophora: a genus of tropical mangrove trees, including the red mangrove
Rhizophora species are easily recognized by their tall, arching prop roots.
survives: continues to live or exist after a difficulty
The old tradition still survives in a few remote mountain villages.
inundated: The low-lying fields were completely inundated after the storm.
props: A wooden beam props up the old barn's leaning roof.
itself: used to refer back to a thing or situation already mentioned, for emphasis
The machine can clean itself without any help from a technician.
above: in or to a higher position than something else
A hawk circled slowly above the quiet valley.
level: a particular amount, height, or standard of something
Water levels rose quickly after three days of heavy rain.
stilt: a tall post or root that raises something above ground or water
The wooden house stood on stilts above the rising flood water.
prop: an object used to support something, or an object used on stage or film
The actor used an umbrella as a prop throughout the entire scene.
then: at that time, or next in a sequence of events
We finished dinner, and then we watched a film together.
absorbs: takes in a liquid or substance gradually
The dry soil quickly absorbs all the spilled water.
air: the invisible mixture of gases surrounding the earth
The mountain air felt crisp and cold after the rain.
lenticels: small pores in bark or stems that allow gas exchange
lỗ vỏ (bì khổng) trên thân cây
Lenticels on the trunk let the tree absorb oxygen from the air.
its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
The cat licked its paw before curling up to sleep.
bark: the tough outer covering of a tree trunk or branch
The bark of the old oak tree was rough and deeply grooved.
black: of the darkest color, like coal or night
She wore a black coat to the formal dinner that evening.
avicennia: a genus of mangrove trees known as black mangroves
Avicennia trees line the muddy banks of the tidal estuary.
germinans: the species name of the black mangrove, Avicennia germinans
Avicennia germinans is commonly known as the black mangrove.
lives: exists or continues to be used
A tradition lives only as long as people keep practising it.
higher: greater in height or degree; comparative of high
Prices are noticeably higher near the tourist areas.
ground: the solid surface of the earth
Leaves covered the ground after the autumn winds.
develops: grows or changes into a more advanced or different state
The patient develops a mild fever a few hours after surgery.
specialized: designed or trained for a particular purpose or area of expertise
The lab uses specialized equipment to test water quality.
root-like: resembling roots in shape or function
The plant developed thin, root-like structures to absorb moisture.
structures: things that have been built, or ways of arranging parts
Termites build remarkably tall structures out of soil and saliva.
pneumatophores: root-like structures that stick up above mud to absorb air
Pneumatophores allow mangrove trees to breathe in waterlogged mud.
stick: to become fixed or attached to a surface
Wet leaves tend to stick to the bottom of your shoes.
out: away from the inside of a place; not in
She stepped out for a few minutes to get some fresh air.
soil: the top layer of earth in which plants grow
Farmers add compost to improve the soil before planting.
like: similar to, or in the same way as
Her handwriting looks a lot like her mother's.
straws: thin hollow tubes, used here as a comparison for root shapes
The children drank their fresh coconut water through bamboo straws.
breathing: the act of taking air into and out of the lungs
Slow, steady breathing can help calm the mind before a test.
tubes: plural of tube; long hollow cylinders
Scientists have found landslides, landers, seismic faults, and even lava tubes on the Moon.
reach: to arrive at or get as far as a place or level
The climbers hoped to reach the summit before the storm arrived.
heights: measurements of how tall something is
The cliffs reach heights of over two hundred meters.
cm: an abbreviation for centimeter, a unit of length
The root grew almost fifteen cm before the frost arrived.
some: an unspecified amount or number of something
Could you buy some bread on your way home?
ft: (viết tắt) feet, đơn vị chiều dài
The tower stands roughly 300 ft above the surrounding plain.
wide: measuring a large distance from side to side
The window between those two outcomes is only a few tens of milliseconds wide.
aerenchyma: plant tissue with air spaces that supplies oxygen to roots
Wetland plants rely on aerenchyma to survive flooded soil.
facilitate: to make an action or process easier
The new software helps facilitate communication between teams.
transport: the movement of people or goods from one place to another
When oil prices rise, transport becomes more expensive for everyone.
because: They cancelled the picnic because it started to rain.
perpetually: The old machine ran perpetually without ever being switched off.
little: There is little time left before the deadline arrives.
free: not fixed or restricted; able to move or act as desired
tự do, không bị ràng buộc
Engineers left a small gap so the metal is free to expand.
available: able to be obtained, used or reached
Tickets for the concert are still available online.
bacteria: Washing your hands removes most of the bacteria on your skin.
liberate: to set free or release something
The chemical reaction can liberate large amounts of heat.
nitrogen: a chemical element that makes up most of Earth's atmosphere
Farmers add nitrogen fertiliser to help crops grow faster.
gas: a substance, like air, that is neither solid nor liquid
Natural gas is commonly used for heating homes.
soluble: able to be dissolved, especially in a liquid
Sugar is highly soluble in warm water.
ferrum: the Latin name for the chemical element iron
The symbol Fe comes from the Latin word ferrum, meaning iron.
iron: a strong, common metal, or a heated device used to smooth clothes
The old gate was made of solid iron and had rusted badly.
inorganic: The soil test measured several inorganic compounds like phosphates.
phosphates: chemical compounds containing phosphorus, often used in fertilizers
Phosphates in fertilizer can run off into nearby rivers.
sulfides: chemical compounds formed when sulfur combines with another element
Hydrogen sulfides give the stagnant swamp its rotten-egg smell.
methane: a colourless, flammable gas that is a major greenhouse gas
Landfill sites release methane as organic waste decomposes.
make: to produce, create or cause something
Good lighting can make a small room feel much larger.
much: to a great extent or degree
The new design does not cost much more than the old one.
less: He eats less meat now than he used to.
nutritious: containing substances the body needs to stay healthy
A nutritious diet helps children grow strong and healthy.
aerial: existing or happening in the air, above ground
Aerial roots let the plant absorb oxygen directly from air.
allow: to let something happen or give permission for it
The new schedule allows students more time for lunch.
absorb: to take in or soak up something such as heat or liquid
Dark clothing tends to absorb more sunlight than pale fabric does.
gases: substances, like air, that are neither solid nor liquid
Greenhouse gases trap heat in the Earth's atmosphere.
directly: in a straight line or manner, without anything in between
You can contact the manager directly if you have a complaint.
atmosphere: the layer of gases surrounding a planet
Carbon dioxide traps heat in the Earth's atmosphere.
nutrients: substances that provide nourishment needed for growth and health
Leafy vegetables are rich in vitamins and other nutrients.
inhospitable: difficult or unpleasant to live in
khắc nghiệt, không thích hợp để sinh sống
Few plants can survive in such an inhospitable desert climate.
inside: the inner part or area of something
The inside of the cave was cool and damp.
processing: the act of treating or preparing something through a series of steps
Food processing can remove much of the fibre found in whole grains.
when: The baker's skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop waiting.
submerged: The old stone bridge remains submerged after weeks of heavy rain.
tide: the regular rise and fall of the sea's surface
The fishing boats returned to shore before the high tide.
